answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a ship paying harbor dues before it may dock at a wharf. The deposit is locked while the agent transacts, and it is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating itself or cheating. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker creating thousands of island identities must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes and quickly exceeds any gain from gaming the market.
